# `•prefs` — Session settings

`•prefs Y` applies the settings in the record `Y` to this session, and returns every setting. The result is shy when `Y` sets something, as an assignment's is. `•prefs ⍬` changes nothing, and shows every setting.

| Setting | Holds | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `box` | `$t` draws matrices, nested arrays and strings in boxes, and leaves other vectors plain | `$t` in the REPL, the BPL Jupyter kernel and IPython once it loads BPL's magics, `$f` elsewhere |
| `trees` | `$t` shows functions and dissected expressions as trees; `$f` uses linear notation. Independent of `box` | as `box` |
| `fns` | `$f` leaves output made inside functions unboxed | as `box` |
| `dissect` | `$t` shows the bound expression before each normal result, using `trees` | `$f` |
| `fusion` | `$t` writes a line for each call that ends a fused computation, as described below | `$f` |
| `limit` | The most items display shows in full. `∞` shows every item | `1000` |
| `edges` | Positions shown at each end of a long axis | `3` |
| `prec` | Significant digits shown for each float. `∞` shows every digit | `10` |
| `width` | The widest line display shows. `∞` allows any width | The terminal's width in the REPL, `∞` elsewhere |
| `notation` | Generated function and operator notation: `"apl"`, `"simplified"` or `"traditional"` | `"apl"` |
| `hanzi_aliases` | `$t` reads hanzi as glyph spellings instead of name characters. Requires a leading declaration on a literal record | `$f` |
| `tolerance` | The relative tolerance of approximate comparison of 64-bit floats, from 0 to `1E¯14`. Narrower floats compare exactly | `1E¯14` |
| `float` | The width of new floats in bits, 16, 32 or 64 | `64` |
| `kinds` | `"static"` makes each result's kind follow from its arguments' kinds and these settings alone. `"dynamic"` lets some functions choose it from values, as described below | `"dynamic"` |
| `int` | The width of integers in bits under static kinds, 32 or 64 | `64` |
| `threads` | The number of threads that large calls split across. `0` gives the default. `1` keeps every call on one thread | `0` |

Display shows part of an array of more than `limit` items: the first and last `edges` positions of each axis longer than twice `edges`. `…` replaces the hidden columns, `⋮` the hidden rows, and `⋱` sits where they cross. A nested array follows the same rule on its own. A line wider than `width` hides columns in the same way, keeping as many at each end as fit. `⎕←` always shows every item, and rounds floats to `prec` as display does. [`⍕`](../glyphs/thorn.qmd) and source text always hold every item and every digit.

`notation` changes generated function and operator displays, including trees and dissected expressions. Dfn source, strings, record keys and field separators stay unchanged. Generated source and structural APIs keep canonical APL spellings.

`hanzi_aliases` controls accepted input independently of `notation`. Put `•prefs ["hanzi_aliases":$t]` before any other code to enable Hanzi glyph spellings. The setting persists across notebook cells and REPL inputs. Loaded files use and update the same preferences as their caller. See [Hanzi spellings](../syntax.qmd#hanzi-spellings).

`tolerance` sets how approximate numbers compare. `x` equals `y` when `|x-y|` is less than the tolerance times the larger magnitude. The setting applies to 64-bit floats. 32-bit and 16-bit floats always compare exactly. Comparison at a tolerance of 0 is exact and faster. A float still stands for a count, a position or a Boolean when it lies within `1E¯14` of one, whatever the setting. [Power](../glyphs/star-diaeresis.qmd) `⍣∞` stops at two results within `1E¯14` of each other, or within 4 units in the last place of a 32-bit or 16-bit float, whatever the setting.

`float` sets the default width of floats, in bits: the width of bare numbers in code parsed after the change, of numbers that `•csv`, `•json`, `•vfi` and `•image` read, of random numbers, and of floats that a function gives from exact arguments. Code already parsed keeps its numbers. A change partway through some code therefore applies from the next input, or from text that [`⍎`](../glyphs/hydrant.qmd) parses later. Leading `•prefs` calls on a literal record are the exception. They run before the rest of their code is parsed, as in the examples below. A script, a notebook cell, a line typed at the REPL, a module that [`•load`](load.qmd) runs and text that `⍎` runs can each set its own width this way. See [Numbers](../numbers.qmd#float-widths).

`kinds` sets whether a result's kind can depend on its arguments' values. Under the default, `"dynamic"`, `√¯4` gives `0ⱼ2`, `1j0` reads as the float `1`, `⌊2.5` gives the exact integer `2`, `7ₓ÷2ₓ` gives `7ᵣ2`, and exact integers grow without limit. Under `"static"`, each result's kind follows from the function, its arguments' kinds and these settings. Real arguments give real results, with NaN outside a function's domain. Complex results stay complex. `⌊`, `⌈` and monadic `×` of floats give floats, and integer `÷` gives floats. Integers compute at the `int` width, or at a wider integer's width, and wrap where a result doesn't fit. Exact fractions stay exact. An integer beside a float takes the float's width. An atom promotes as an array does. Fused computations and a GPU need each result's kind before they run, and under static kinds more calls fuse, as the examples under `fusion` show. A literal reads under the settings in force when its code is parsed, as with `float`. See [Numbers](../numbers.qmd#static-kinds).

`threads` sets how many threads this session's large calls split across. A call splits only when it has enough work to repay the extra threads. Float results can differ in their last bits between thread counts. The default, 0, uses the number in the `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` environment variable where it's set, and one thread for each core otherwise. 1 runs every call on the thread that evaluates the code. When several BPL processes run at once, such as a pool of Python workers, set 1 in each of them to keep them from competing for the cores. The browser build runs every call on one thread, whatever the setting.

`fusion` shows where large computations stop waiting. Calls of these glyphs on large arrays of floats run together, block by block, reading each array once: monadic `+ - ÷ | * π ⊼ ⊽ ≤ ≥`, and dyadic `+ - × ÷ | ⌈ ⌊ π` and the comparisons. Structural functions such as `⌽`, `⍉`, `↑`, `↓` and `↕` on large arrays of any kind wait too, as a map of their argument. Each call waits until something reads its result. Fused calls, reductions, other pervasive calls and `+.×` read a waiting structural result through its map, without building it. A read of a few items computes only those items. Any other reader computes the whole result first, such as `⍋`, display, and Python conversions other than NumPy views of structural results. With `fusion` set to `$t`, the innermost call that computes items of a waiting result writes a line naming its function and position, such as `fusion ends at ⍋ (<input>:1:46)`. A reduction such as `+/` of a waiting result runs with the calls and writes nothing.

[`•explain`](explain.qmd) records the same events. In the first example, the comparison runs with the arithmetic and `+/`. In the second, monadic `⌊` ends the fusion of `y×2`:

```bpl
y←¿1000000⍴0
(•explain "+/(y+1)<|y-0.5").fused.glyphs    ⍝ ["-|+<+/"]
(•explain "+/⌊y×2").forced.function         ⍝ ["⌊"]
```

A call fuses when its result is floats of its arguments' width, or Booleans, and it can't fail. This example checks the list above against the monadic and dyadic forms of each numeric glyph. Halves of small integers keep `∨` and `∧` quick. Under static kinds, every monadic glyph in the list fuses except `○`, whose results are complex. There, the kernels give NaN or floats where dynamic kinds would rerun a call on complex numbers or give integers, so they can't fail:

```bpl
y←0.5×¿200000⍴100
fuses←{0<≢(•explain ⍵).fused.glyphs}
monads←"+-×÷|⌈⌊*⍟√!○π⊼⊽≤≥"
dyads←"+-×÷|⌈⌊*⍟√!π∨∧=≠<≤>≥"
({fuses "+/",⍵,"y"}¨monads)#monads      ⍝ "+-÷|*π⊼⊽≤≥"
({fuses "+/0.5",⍵,"y"}¨dyads)#dyads     ⍝ "+-×÷|⌈⌊π=≠<≤>≥"
•prefs ["kinds":"static"] ⋄ ({fuses "+/",⍵,"y"}¨monads)#monads    ⍝ "+-×÷|⌈⌊*⍟√!π⊼⊽≤≥"
•prefs ["kinds":"dynamic"]
```

```bpl
•prefs ["tolerance":0] ⋄ 0.3=0.1+0.2    ⍝ $f
•prefs ["tolerance":1E¯14] ⋄ 0.3=0.1+0.2    ⍝ $t
•prefs ["tolerance":1E¯14] ⋄ 1ₛ=1.0000001ₛ    ⍝ $f
•prefs ["float":32] ⋄ (•storage 1.5).kind    ⍝ "float32"
•prefs ["float":64] ⋄ (•storage 1.5).kind    ⍝ "float64"
•prefs ["threads":1] ⋄ "threads"⊃•prefs ⍬    ⍝ 1ₓ
•prefs ["kinds":"static"] ⋄ √¯4    ⍝ $n
•prefs ["kinds":"static" "int":32] ⋄ 2147483647ₓ+1ₓ    ⍝ ¯2147483648ₓ
•prefs ["kinds":"dynamic" "int":64] ⋄ √¯4    ⍝ 0ⱼ2
```

Errors: `DOMAIN` for an unknown setting or an invalid value. Under static kinds, `LIMIT` for an exact integer literal that doesn't fit the `int` width, or for a count or position that doesn't fit it.
